[[File:Imperialriottrooper-FU2.jpg|thumb|An Imperial riot trooper on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]].]]
{{Quote|I swear this sacred oath that I shall render unconditional obedience to Emperor Palpatine, to exercise every power in service to the Galactic Empire, and shall, whensoever I am asked, be prepared, as a loyal servant, to surrender my life for this oath.|The Oath of Obedience|<ref name="TFU II">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]''</ref>}}
'''Riot Stormtroopers''', colloquially known as '''Riot troopers''', were highly-trained [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] that specialized in containing and defusing insurrectionist scenarios<ref name="Death Star">[[Death Star (novel)|''Death Star'']]</ref> due to the spread of the influence of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] to even within loyalist populations in the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="IMB">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref> As [[Imperial Military/Legends|military]] enforcers of the Empire, the riot troopers were typically stationed on subjugated [[Planet/Legends|worlds]] throughout the [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]], such as [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] and [[Cato Neimoidia/Legends|Cato Neimoidia]], although they were most common on megalopolis worlds throughout the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core]] and [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]] due to them being disobedient worlds, that according to the Empire, required "parental discipline."<ref name="IMB" /> They were trained for close-combat, and thus were armed with [[Electrostaff/Legends|electrostaffs]], made from [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]]-resistant [[Cortosis/Legends|cortosis]]. As a consequence, they lacked any type of range weapon. In addition to their weapons, the riot troopers wore protective suits that slightly resembled the [[Stormtrooper/Legends|armor]] of the [[Stormtrooper/Legends|Imperial stormtroopers]].<ref name="TFU II" />

The riot troopers' special status was emphasised by the fact that they received training at an [[Imperial Royal Guard Academy]] on [[Yinchorr/Legends|Yinchorr]], the same facility where [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] [[Emperor's Royal Guard/Legends|Royal Guardsmen]] were trained. Every riot trooper was required to swear the [[Oath of Obedience]] upon graduation as a symbol of their unquestioning loyalty to the Emperor and his Empire&mdash;an oath that could only be severed through [[Death/Legends|death]]. In combat, they were often accompanied by a squad of stormtroopers; the troopers provided aid from a distance with their range weapons while the riot troopers closed in on the enemy with their electrostaffs.<ref name="TFU II" /> Because they were trained specifically for confronting and putting down large-scale civilian insurrections, they lacked any fear of being overwhelmed by crowds. However, when faced with direct weaponized conflict, riot troopers were forced to call in standard stormtroopers.<ref name="IMB" />

In [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], roughly a year into the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], several riot troopers were killed, along with many other Imperial [[Trooper/Legends|troopers]], in the [[Timira City]] Cloning Facility of Kamino. Six months after the formation of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] commissioned a clandestine project to recreate his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|fallen apprentice]], the late [[Galen Marek]], through an experimental type of [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoan]] [[Cloning/Legends|cloning technology]]. However, the procedure was initially imperfect and resulted in [[Aberrant clone|numerous abject failures]], including an emotionally unstable [[Subject 1138|clone]] who [[Escape from Kamino (1 BBY)|escaped]] from Kamino. During his break out, many riot troopers attempted to neutralize the rogue clone's progress, but were ultimately killed for their efforts. Although they were able to defend themselves against the clone's dual lightsabers, they were completely helpless against his genetically-inherited [[Force power/Legends|Force powers]]. For all of their weapons and training, they were no match against the clone's [[Force-sensitive/Legends|command]] of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].<ref name="TFU II" />

The rogue clone of the original Starkiller later again fought against more Imperial riot troopers on [[Cato Neimoidia/Legends|Cato Neimoidia]], shortly after his escape from Kamino. He intended to [[Rescue of Rahm Kota|rescue]] [[Jedi General/Legends|General]] [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]], a member of the Rebel Alliance and Marek's [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi mentor]], from the [[Tarko-se/Legends|Tarko-se]] [[Tarko-se Arena|Arena]]. The entire Imperial garrison in Tarko-se, including many riot troopers, attempted to kill the clone before he could reach the city; many of them were killed, and the clone ultimately succeeded in his mission.<ref name="TFU II" />

During the [[Assault on Kamino]], many riot troopers were part of the planet's Imperial military defense force. The riot troopers on Timira City, however, were defeated easily by the renegade clone, who was forced to return to his homeworld in order to rescue [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Juno Eclipse/Legends|Juno Eclipse]]. The combination of Rebel ground assault forces and the clone of Galen Marek were too much for the riot troopers to contain. Hence, they failed in their duty to prevent the fall of Timira City and the capture of Darth Vader.<ref name="TFU II" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Riot stormtrooper was created for the video game ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]'' in [[2010]], but wasn't identified under that name until the release of ''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]'' in [[2014]]. The troopers were voiced by [[Fred Tatasciore]].
